title: Points, Vertices and Primitives in POPs
summary: Official Derivative page describing POP points, vertices, and primitives, including supported primitive types, line strips, point primitives, the current mesh limitation in POPs, and invisible point-list-without-primitive cases.
key_concepts: Meshes - NOT IMPLEMENTED IN POPS ATM
guidance: Use this article when a POP plan needs to choose point primitives, line strips, triangle/quad surfaces, or no-render point lists for instancing and copy-template workflows.
Every POP has a point list, and every primitive usually has vertices that index into that point list.
Plan triangle, quad, line, linestrip, or point primitives for POP topology; arbitrary closed polygons, curve primitives, and SOP-style mesh primitives are not implemented in POPs.
A closed linestrip connects the last vertex back to the first, but it is not a filled polygon.
A POP can have a point list with no primitives; those points will not render directly, but can still be useful for instancing, copy templates, and data workflows.
Use Point Sprite MAT when point primitives should render as dots or sprites.
